title: Can I BEAT Gambonanza?
summary: Gambonanza: a chess roguelike on a small board. A run starts with a piece-wheel spin (Tony gets two kings and a rook), then 5 escalating fights against enemy piece sets (2 pawns, 5 pawns, ...) ending with a boss (a Judit Polgár pun). Captures and wins earn money ($) spent in a shop on gambits (e.g. Church's Gambit: +$2 per bishop at game start; Will-o'-the-Wisp's Gambit: captures on white tiles have 1/3 chance to create a phantom tile that copies pieces), chess/tile/gambit tokens, a queen ($10), re-rolls and extra board slots. Boards have modified tiles, holes and falling tiles. Tony beats the first boss, continues into a later round and loses when a tile his piece relied on didn't fall in time.
rules: Roguelike run: piece wheel gives starting pieces; you may place ('prepare your strategy') your pieces before each fight.
Each run segment is 5 games of increasing difficulty; game 5 is a boss fight.
Earn $ per win and per captured piece; spend between games on gambits, tokens, pieces (queen $10), re-rolls and max-piece upgrades.
Board is a mini board with special tiles: holes/gaps block movement, some tiles fall after a delay (a piece on a falling tile is lost), modified tiles from tokens.
You can field multiple kings; losing condition is losing all/required pieces (exact rule unclear).
win_condition: Clear every fight (capture all enemy pieces / checkmate) through the boss; video run ends in defeat after the first boss.
